title: TCL's IFA 2026 showcase bags over 30 global honors

blocks.text: Walking into TCL’s showcase at IFA 2026, it was difficult to look at any one product without appreciating the wholistic impact of it all.

The company had built its presentation around the idea of a connected home, with televisions, phones, appliances, smart glasses and AI-powered devices occupying different parts of the same experience. Rather than treating each product as a separate announcement, TCL presented them as pieces of a larger ecosystem.
TCL received more than 30 honors at this year’s show, including seven IFA Innovation Award Honoree recognitions and five Global Product Technology Innovation Awards.

The televisions were among the most prominent products in the lineup. The TCL X11L SQD-Mini LED TV received Android Authority’s IFA Breakthrough 2026 Award and Tom’s Guide’s Best in Show Award, with the recognition centered on TCL’s SQD-Mini LED technology. The C8L SQD-Mini LED TV was also named an IFA Innovation Award Honoree, while the X3 Series OLED+ Gaming Monitor received the same distinction for its contrast, refresh rates and design.

The display focus fits naturally into TCL’s broader approach at IFA. Rather than presenting its TVs as standalone products, the company placed them within a larger connected-home environment where screens, appliances and other devices are designed to work together. That approach was also reflected in the range of products surrounding the televisions, from smartphones and wearables to home appliances.

The smartphone lineup was led by the P80 Series, which received Android Authority’s Best of IFA 2026 Award. The flagship P80 Ultra also received an IFA Innovation Award Honoree recognition for its camera system, display and design.

TCL’s RayNeo smart glasses brought another part of the company’s hardware portfolio into the showcase. The RayNeo iO Smart Glasses were recognized by the IFA Innovation Awards for their integrated AI assistant. The RayNeo GT Max AR Glasses received both an IFA Innovation Award Honoree recognition and a Global Product Technology Innovation Award for what TCL describes as the world’s first Dolby Vision-certified AR experience.

The company’s push into AI also extends beyond personal devices. TCL’s Solar Series Air Conditioner, TwinMag Prime Fresh Series Refrigerator and heyAiMe Family Companion Robot each received a Global Product Technology Innovation Award. The TCL 5G AI CPE X5 Router was named an IFA Innovation Award Honoree for its agentic features.

Alongside the product awards, TCL used IFA to highlight work around display standards. The company and TÜV Rheinland jointly published the SQD-Mini LED Display Industry White Paper, which proposes a framework for evaluating display performance under different real-world viewing conditions. TCL also received what it describes as the world’s first SGS Natural Light Visual Comfort Certification, based on a standard it developed with SGS.

The collection of awards gives TCL plenty to point to at IFA 2026, but the more interesting part of the showcase is how the different pieces of its portfolio fit together. The company is no longer presenting its display business separately from its work in appliances, mobile devices, AI and connected-home products. TCL’s broader commitment to advancing next- generation technologies and bringing smarter, more intuitive experiences into everyday life was on full display.
